teaser: You give Claude hands: built-in Read, Edit and Bash tools, then your first @tool that checks stock and reports errors back to Claude.
takeaways: Claude emits a ToolUseBlock; the SDK runs hooks and permission checks, executes the tool and returns a ToolResultBlock.
Tool failures reach Claude as is_error results, not exceptions in your app; Claude decides whether to retry or change approach.
Custom tools use @tool(name, description, input_schema) + create_sdk_mcp_server, run in-process, and are named mcp__<server>__<tool>.
Bash is the highest-risk built-in; readOnlyHint tools can run in parallel; mcp__github__* wildcards are valid but a global * is ignored.
